I am proud to lead with @RepHoulahan & @RepSpanberger the bipartisan, bicameral Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act, which will require the federal Election Assistance Commission (EAC) to develop guidelines for election administrators on both the uses and the risks of artificial intelligence. We must continue, amidst technological advances, to ensure the public trust and the integrity of our elections.

With the growing potential for artificial intelligence to be utilized in elections, it is essential that state and local officials are prepared, and that they are provided with the resources they need to keep our elections secure.

Our legislation will shield the American people from the dangers of deceptive AI-generated content, ensuring our elections remain free, fair, and true to the will of the American people. This is not a partisan or controversial issue—it’s about restoring faith and upholding the trust that voters place in our democracy, a commitment I will never waver from.

In a major victory for animals, patients, and science, the @US_FDA is finally beginning to move away from outdated animal testing.

This has been a top priority of my Congressional Animal Protection Caucus that I’ve co-chaired since joining Congress—and today, after persistent bipartisan advocacy, real change is happening.

The FDA will now allow advanced, human-based alternatives—like AI models, organoids, and global data—to replace animal testing for monoclonal antibody therapies.

This means:

✅ Fewer dogs, primates, and other animals used in testing
✅ Faster, safer treatments for patients
✅ Lower drug development costs

This is a smarter, more compassionate path forward—and one we’ve been fighting for, every step of the way.

In an age where personal privacy — and the safety of our kids — can be violated with a click, tonight’s House passage of the bipartisan TAKE IT DOWN Act marks a critical step forward.

This legislation creates long-overdue federal safeguards against non-consensual intimate imagery and the growing threat of AI-generated deepfakes. It establishes a clear legal standard: victims, especially children, have the right to have these exploitative images removed — and perpetrators will be held accountable.

This is a commonsense, essential measure to protect our families, empower survivors, and bring our laws in line with the realities of the digital era.

American elections should belong to the American people—no loopholes, no exceptions. But right now, foreign nationals can still fund state and local ballot initiatives. That’s a threat to our democracy—and we’re putting a stop to it. 

Today, @RepGolden and I introduced the bipartisan Stop Foreign Funds in Elections Act to ban foreign contributions in all taxpayer-funded elections—federal, state, and local—ensuring they’re free from foreign manipulation at every level.

This is part of a broader fight I’m leading to restore trust in our democracy—ensuring every U.S. citizen, regardless of party, has the right to vote in every taxpayer-funded election; ending congressional stock trading; banning deceptive deepfake ads; and dismantling partisan gerrymandering once and for all.

Because defending democracy means action—and I’ll keep fighting to make sure it works for the people, not special interests or foreign powers.

Big news for PA-1! 

@amazon is making a historic $20 billion investment in Pennsylvania—including a flagship, state-of-the-art data center campus right here in Bucks County. This transformational project will create over 1,250 high-paying, high-tech jobs, bring advanced AI and cloud infrastructure to our region, and launch hands-on workforce training programs that connect our students and workers to the industries of the future.

I’ve long worked to position Bucks County as a hub for innovation and economic growth, and I was proud to support this initiative to strengthen our workforce, grow our economy, and build a more competitive future for our community and country.  

I look forward to working with both labor and business to make this investment a huge success in our community. 🇺🇸

In recent weeks, I’ve had conversation after conversation with constituents sounding the alarm on the same issue: robocalls and scam texts are out of control. 

So today, I delivered a communication to Attorney General Bondi demanding clear action from the Department of Justice to crack down on this growing wave of fraud. These scams are targeting our seniors, veterans, and financially vulnerable neighbors—and we need a whole-of-government response to stop them.

In my letter, I pressed DOJ to:

➡️ Detail what’s currently being done to combat fraudulent robocalls
➡️ Identify gaps in authority or resources that Congress can address
➡️ Explain how they’re coordinating with the FCC, FTC, and state leaders

This is part of a broader push I’m leading in Congress to protect consumers and hold bad actors accountable, including:

✅ The QUIET Act – to expose AI-generated robocalls and toughen penalties
✅ The STOP Scammers Act – to hit foreign scam networks where it hurts

This isn’t just about nuisance calls—it’s about protecting our people from exploitation. 

Read my full letter below. ⬇️

We’ll also be partnering on the transformational Amazon data center project coming to Falls Township—part of a $20 billion investment that will create over 1,250 high-tech jobs, build cutting-edge cloud and AI infrastructure, and launch hands-on workforce training right here in Bucks County.

This is a pivotal opportunity for our community, and I’m looking forward to continuing working with Mike and Exelon to make it a success—strengthening our economy, expanding opportunity, and ensuring affordable, reliable energy for the road ahead.

When a project has the power to reshape our region, it is critical to bring everyone to the table.

This project will:

It was the kind of conversation that drives progress and shapes policy—labor and business at the same table, having honest dialogue, and a united focus on leading in innovation and American competitiveness, powered by local labor. 

Thank you to Nicole Levine (Senior VP & COO, PECO), Marie Dixon (Senior VP, Federal Affairs, Exelon), Becky Ford, Merle Madrid, and Judd Smith from Amazon, and all our amazing local Building Trades leaders representing 15 local unions, for your insights, your partnership, and your passion, and your love of America.  I look forward to continuing our partnership together as Bucks County once again leads the way in building America’s future.

🚨 Lyme disease is surging across Bucks and Montgomery Counties—and Pennsylvania now accounts for nearly 30% of all cases nationwide.

This isn’t a surprise. It’s the result of years of warnings that went unheeded. That’s why I’ve been working with local health officials, scientists, and national advocates to lead a strong, sustained federal response.

Here’s what we’re doing:

I’m leading a bipartisan push to modernize how our country prevents, detects, treats, and responds to tick-borne illnesses, including:

✅ Kay Hagan TICK Act Reauthorization – To reestablish a coordinated national strategy
✅ LymeX Authorization Act – To accelerate innovation in diagnostics and treatments
✅ Children Inflicted by Lyme Disabilities Act – To expand protections for kids with chronic Lyme
✅ BITE Act – Creates an AI-powered tick outbreak alert system
✅ Tick Identification Pilot Program – Supports state-level photo-based tracking programs

I’ve also fought to expand Lyme research funding through both the Defense and Health Appropriations bills, to ensure science gets the investment it needs.

But until there’s a cure, prevention is key. As we head into Lyme Disease Awareness Month, here’s how to protect yourself and your family:

• Use EPA-registered repellents (DEET, picaridin, IR3535, oil of lemon eucalyptus)
• Wear light-colored clothing and tuck in your pants/shirt
• Shower within 2 hours of outdoor activity
• Do a full-body tick check—especially behind knees, underarms, hairline, waistband 
• Check pets and gear—ask your vet about year-round tick preventatives

⚠️ Watch for symptoms:
• Bullseye rash (may not always appear)
• Fever, chills, fatigue, joint pain
• In kids: memory issues, joint aches, behavioral changes

🕒 Early detection is key. The sooner it’s caught, the easier it is to treat.

When it comes to end-of-life care, compassion and policy must go hand in hand.

Yesterday, I had a great meeting with the incredible Tina and Erik Krajnikovich, owners of Vitality Hospice in Langhorne, and members of their exceptional care team, to discuss realities facing our local community-based hospice providers. 

We covered the real-world impact of federal hospice regulations, from rising compliance demands and escalating audits, to the challenges of navigating policy changes as a smaller, mission-driven provider. We also explored the future of care at the intersection of AI and healthcare, and how smart, responsible policy must ensure that technology enhances, not replaces, the personal care that defines hospice.

I’m grateful to Tina, Erik, and the Vitality team for their partnership and service to our community. Their insights will continue shaping my work to deliver thoughtful, balanced reforms that protect patients, support caregivers, and keep compassion at the center of care.

America is a nation of laws and a nation of immigrants. Not one or the other—both. These principles define our story and shape our responsibility to the future. Meeting that responsibility requires leadership, not gridlock.

For too long, Washington has chosen division over solutions. The @ProbSolveCaucus is working to change that, advancing a bipartisan framework to secure the border, modernize the system, and uphold both the rule of law and America’s proud immigrant heritage.

Today, @RepTomSuozzi and I met with Steve DeAngelis—Founder & CEO of Enterra Solutions, internationally recognized leader in AI and advanced analytics, and our own PA-1 constituent—to discuss how advanced technology can strengthen border security, disrupt trafficking networks, and support lasting reform.

I’m grateful to Steve for his insights and partnership in ensuring America remains both secure and true to its ideals through innovation.

Great meeting with @LaSalleUniv President Daniel Allen and @Bucks_edu President Patrick Jones to advance a key shared priority: preparing our students to succeed in tomorrow’s workforce.

Employer needs are evolving quickly—particularly in foreign language proficiency, AI, and international business. Our discussion centered on aligning degree pathways and strengthening collaboration between two-year and four-year programs to meet those needs with intention.

We also talked about expanding a Washington, D.C. internship pipeline to give local students first-hand exposure to public policy, national service, and career paths they may have never envisioned for themselves.

Thank you to Presidents Allen and Jones for your continued partnership. I look forward to building on this work together and ensuring every student has access to the tools, training, and opportunities needed to lead in a global, technology-driven economy.

This was more than a cyber breach—it was a warning shot. A reported Chinese state-sponsored group used AI to autonomously execute an espionage operation—rapid targeting, independent execution, almost no human touchpoints—showing just how quickly the battlefield is evolving and why we must stay ahead.

From my work in the FBI to my role leading CIA oversight on the House Intelligence Committee, I know AI security cannot sit on the margins of our national defense strategy—it must be a core requirement. This incident makes that unmistakably clear. We must bring the full weight of our national security apparatus to this challenge and ensure the United States stays ahead of any adversary seeking to weaponize AI.

What a year it has been. 

From fighting for our community at home to advancing two-party solutions and defending freedom abroad, this captures only a portion of the work we've done this year—the work guided by one constant: you.

In 2025, we delivered for PA-1:

✅ 47.5M recovered and returned to our families
✅ 5,912 constituent cases resolved
✅126,000 letters and emails sent
✅ 67 bills introduced
✅ Nearly 800 bills co-sponsored—more than any other Representative
✅ 40 co-sponsored bills passed the House

Behind every number is a neighbor, but numbers alone don't tell the full story.

The rest of the work unfolded in living rooms, at kitchen tables, and conversations here at home and in Washington—listening, learning, and working with you.

After years of standing together, we delivered justice for our public servants. Through the Social Security Fairness Act—which I was proud to help lead and see signed into law—we restored full, hard-earned benefits for police officers, firefighters, teachers, and public servants who had been shortchanged for far too long.

When the Sunoco pipeline leak upended life in Upper Makefield, I worked with residents and the Mt. Eyre Task Force to demand accountability, confront failure, and turn it into reform. Together, we authored the bipartisan Wojnovich Pipeline Safety Act—legislation to enact the strongest pipeline safety protections in over a decade.

When Head Start funding was threatened, I worked with the Bucks County Intermediate Unit to intervene immediately, pressing federal decision-makers at every level, securing both an emergency extension and a full five-year renewal to protect a vital lifeline for working families and give our children the fair start they deserve.

Through roundtables here at home and in Washington, we ensured local voices were driving national conversations on Medicare, SNAP, cost-of-living pressures, and more. We brought together local labor, business, and community leaders, to help move forward one of the most transformative investments Bucks County has seen—creating union jobs, expanding opportunity, and positioning our region to lead in innovation with the new AI data center in Falls Township.

And beyond our borders, we fought to stand with our allies, and advance peace through strength, because the safety of our families at home is tied to America’s leadership abroad.

As we look toward 2026, the work before us continues. But history has shown, time and again, when we stand together, progress is not a matter of chance—it is a matter of time. That is the American way, and it remains the only path forward.

Artificial intelligence presents enormous opportunity and equally serious questions, and neither political party has a monopoly on the answers. Our challenge is to embrace innovation without abandoning responsibility—to protect workers, strengthen our national security, preserve accountability, and ensure America continues to lead the world.

As artificial intelligence advances, our laws must keep pace. I’m grateful to my colleagues in the Problem Solvers Caucus for supporting this commonsense bipartisan effort to protect victims and close dangerous gaps in federal law.

Making AI benefit American workers is not only a matter of fairness, but is essential to U.S. global competitiveness, economic leadership, and long-term security. Artificial intelligence can support innovation, new industries, and expanded opportunity, but its impact will ultimately be determined by the working people whose skill and judgment put those tools to use.

AI must work for American workers—not the other way around.

If America is going to lead the world in artificial intelligence, we must also lead in ensuring that progress strengthens—not sidelines—the people who make this country work.

That’s why I called on the Administration, alongside @SenMarkKelly, to adopt a worker-centered AI strategy grounded in transparency, accountability, human oversight, and a meaningful role for the workers whose skill and judgment will determine whether this technology fulfills its promise.

Innovation and worker protection go hand in hand, and I will always fight to ensure our hardworking men and women are protected, empowered, and fully represented in the future they are helping build.

@AFLCIO @PaAFL_CIO

The road to a stronger America runs through the men and women who keep it moving.

What a great morning with the Pennsylvania Conference of @Teamsters and my good friend President Bill Hamilton.

Our work together is focused on action: passing the American Energy Dominance Act, built with labor to strengthen American energy and support good-paying union jobs; advancing the Faster Labor Contracts Act so a vote to organize leads to a fair first contract without endless delay; continuing the fight for the PRO Act; strengthening workplace safety and training; and making sure workers are at the table as AI reshapes the future of work.

Thank you to the PA Teamsters—especially from our PA-1 community—for your leadership, friendship, and all you do to drive our nation forward. 

Together, we’ll continue fighting for a future where workers’ rights are protected, their voices are heard, and their essential role in America’s strength is reflected in the policies we pass.

What a great morning with my friends from the Lower Bucks County Chamber of Commerce for our annual State of the Nation address.

At a time of rising costs, workforce pressures, rapid technological change, and real uncertainty for families and businesses, the voice of our local economy has never been more important.

Today’s conversation focused on what it will take to compete and grow—lowering costs, strengthening our workforce, improving access to care, securing reliable energy, preparing for AI, and keeping Bucks County businesses strong in a changing world.

Thank you to Executive Director Lisa Pflaumer, the entire LBCCC team, and everyone who joined us today. I am grateful for your partnership and for the work you do every day to serve our business community, create opportunity, and move Lower Bucks forward.

When the Zezzo family of Bucks County came to me after their teenage daughter endured years of cyberstalking, we turned their experience into action. I authored the bipartisan Combat Online Predators Act, strengthening penalties for those who stalk minors and improving enforcement—and in 2020, it became law.

Since then, working alongside advocates, law enforcement, and families across our community, we are seeing a new dimension of that same challenge. AI-powered license-plate reader systems like Flock can help law enforcement identify vehicles tied to criminal activity, but documented cases show the technology has also been used to track women, former partners, and others for unauthorized purposes.

Now, I’m calling on the Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission to establish clear federal standards for their use. Law enforcement should have every effective tool it needs to protect our communities—but technology this powerful must come with equally strong safeguards against abuse.

Read the full letter below ⬇️

For months, along with my colleagues from both sides of the aisle, we have been developing serious, bipartisan frameworks to strengthen the safeguards around advanced AI.

Now it is time to move that work forward.

We’re now calling on House leadership to advance the dozens of bipartisan bills already on the table to strengthen AI security, transparency, and independent oversight—and better protect the systems our country depends on.

When the risks are clear and responsible solutions are within reach, inaction carries consequences of its own. We should not wait for a crisis to force the decisions we are capable of making today.

Families across Bucks and Montgomery Counties should not be asked to pay higher electric bills to cover the massive infrastructure costs created by some of the largest companies in the world. [...] America can lead in innovation without shifting the cost of that growth onto working families, seniors, and small businesses.

As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the national security risks—from threats to critical infrastructure to dangerous miscalculation in a crisis.

Ahead of Xi’s visit today, our Problem Solvers Caucus AI and Evolving Technologies Working Group called on the Adminstrarion to implement a coordinated international framework on AI safety and security—anchored in American standards for testing and incident reporting, stronger infrastructure protections, and firm safeguards against AI-enabled cyber aggression.

The rules governing advanced AI are being written now. America should shape them before our adversaries do—and ensure they protect our security, strength, and technological leadership.

Read our letter below ⬇️
The United States leads the world in AI, and we intend to keep it that way. But if we do not lead in setting global standards for advanced AI development, our adversaries will.
